subject: Physics
chapter: Chapter 6: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
central_question: How can the motion and equilibrium of extended bodies be described using centre of mass, torque, moment of inertia and angular momentum?
in_scope_units: 6.1 Introduction and 6.1.1 kinds of rigid-body motion — translation, rotation and their combination.
6.4 Linear momentum of a system of particles.
6.6 Angular velocity and its relation with linear velocity, including angular acceleration.
6.8 Equilibrium of a rigid body, principle of moments and centre of gravity.
6.9 Moment of inertia and radius of gyration.
6.10 Kinematics of rotational motion about a fixed axis.
6.11 Dynamics of rotational motion about a fixed axis.
6.12 Angular momentum for rotation about a fixed axis and conservation of angular momentum.
banned_topics: Work–energy chapter treatment unrelated to rotational analogies

known_pitfalls.claim: In pure translation different particles of a rigid body can have different velocities at the same instant.
known_pitfalls.correction: In pure translational motion, all particles of the rigid body have the same velocity at any instant.

known_pitfalls.claim: Internal forces determine the acceleration of the centre of mass.
known_pitfalls.correction: Internal forces cancel in pairs in the system equation; M A_CM equals the net external force.
a × b = −b × a, so reversing the order reverses the direction.

known_pitfalls.claim: A rigid body is in equilibrium if only the net force is zero.
known_pitfalls.correction: Mechanical equilibrium requires both net external force zero and net external torque zero.

known_pitfalls.claim: Moment of inertia depends only on total mass.
known_pitfalls.correction: It depends on how the mass is distributed relative to the chosen axis.
